question: Hermes taskpool final_landed gate final implementation plan: prevent false auto-close of user-approved manual-review reopened tasks while allowing true final implementation evidence.

context.problem: Hermes taskpool manual-review reopened tasks were falsely auto-closed again as done using weak evidence such as py_compile_taskpool PASS, proof hashes, and PASS_ADVISORY_ONLY/advisory artifacts. User approved fixing according to final plan with real multi-model analysis.

observed_incident.T02: done -> pending after manual review, then auto-closed back to done using py_compile/hash/multimodel-only evidence; manually corrected to blocked
observed_incident.T04: same false close recurrence; manually corrected to blocked
observed_incident.T17: retry after agent-team human escape release; not complete
observed_incident.control_plane: selfcheck PASS and proof-check PASS, so the issue is semantic closeout gating rather than global health

current_code.current_final_landed_hook: completion_gate_failures appends manual_review_final_landed=false failure when task_requires_final_landed_evidence(task) and not evidence_has_final_landed_signal(evidence)
current_code.current_risk: evidence_has_final_landed_signal is token-based and accepts broad tokens such as commit/skill/script/config/test/verification anywhere in the evidence blob; it may accept weak or incidental text rather than a structured feature-specific implementation+verification bundle.
current_code.relevant_lines: FINAL_LANDED_EVIDENCE_TOKENS lines 3533-3551; task_requires_final_landed_evidence 3554-3560; completion_gate_failures 3568-3614; lifecycle_gate calls completion_gate_failures at 3879-3880; auto-close-review probes lifecycle_gate before closing around 4681-4682.

existing_tests.gap: No RED test yet proves that one weak incidental token, e.g. command:pytest PASS alone or file path containing config, cannot satisfy final_landed for approve_reopen/needs_more_evidence.

desired_final_plan_candidate.rule: For manual_review_final_landed=false tasks whose approval action is not approve_close_as_partial/approve_watch, done requires a structured final-landed bundle, not a substring token.
desired_final_plan_candidate.bundle_shape: At least one implementation artifact evidence (commit OR script/code/config/skill file path/artifact) AND at least one verification evidence (test/pytest/vitest/benchmark/read-back/browser/curl/selfcheck/proof-check tied to the implementation). Weak evidence classes such as py_compile_taskpool, proof:sha256 only, PASS_ADVISORY_ONLY, ExperienceAtom-only, generic manual-review report, or advisory discussion artifacts remain insufficient.
desired_final_plan_candidate.closeout_path: Apply in lifecycle_gate -> completion_gate_failures so transition done and auto-close-review both fail closed. Keep approve_close_as_partial and approve_watch closable as partial/watch outcomes. Keep blocked T02/T04 until gate is committed and verified.

constraints: No feature loss, no precision loss; fail closed for ambiguous evidence.
Use TDD: add failing regression before production patch.
Do not broaden expensive multimodel autorun; this is deterministic lifecycle gating.
Preserve partial close/watch exceptions because those are explicit non-final outcomes.
Hermes own changes need scoped git commit in ~/.hermes.
context.question: Critique the candidate final plan and return a concise final implementation recommendation. Should the gate be simple token-based or structured bundle-based? What exact evidence classes should block/allow, and where should it be enforced?

constraints: fail closed for approve_reopen/needs_more_evidence manual-review tasks when evidence is advisory-only, py_compile-only, proof-hash-only, or incidental substring-only
preserve approve_close_as_partial and approve_watch as non-final closeout exceptions
